description: Hand-labelled bug reports for evaluating the decision model against the default triage guidance (SIMPLE: fewer than 5 files and no new architectural pattern, external dependency, data-model change or cross-service contract change). Labels are the author's judgement for the todo-service demo repository. Several SIMPLE cases are written in alarming language and several COMPLEX cases in mild language, to test whether the model confuses severity with scope.

cases.text:
BUG-001 — Build is broken: npm run build fails with TS2345

Running npm run build fails:
src/todos.ts: error TS2345: Argument of type 'TodoRow | undefined' is not assignable to parameter of type 'TodoRow'.

The project no longer compiles, which blocks every deployment. The failure was introduced with the completeTodo change that made the row lookup return an optional value.

Expected: npm run build succeeds and completeTodo returns undefined for a non-existent todo id (the HTTP layer already handles that case with a 404).

BUG-002 — SQL injection in todo search endpoint

The GET /todos/search?q=... endpoint builds its SQL query by string concatenation with the raw user-supplied search term. A crafted q parameter can change the query structure (classic SQL injection), e.g. q=%' OR '1'='1 returns every row regardless of the search term.

Expected: the search term is passed to the database as a bound parameter (parameterized query), never concatenated into the SQL string. Search behavior for normal terms must not change.
BUG-010 — The 404 response for a missing todo says 'Todo not foud'. Fix the typo to 'Todo not found' in src/server.ts.
BUG-011 — GET /todos?limit=10 returns 11 rows. The limit handling in src/todos.ts adds one to the requested limit. Expected: exactly `limit` rows.
BUG-012 — GET /todos/abc returns 500 because the id is not validated. Validate that :id is a positive integer in src/server.ts and return 400 otherwise.
BUG-013 — DELETE /todos/:id returns 200 when the todo does not exist. It should return 404, like GET does.
DOC-3 — The README says to run npm start, but the script is npm run dev. Update the README.

SEV-1 PRODUCTION OUTAGE — the service crashes on startup with TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'port') in src/server.ts. Every request fails and customers are down. The config key was renamed from serverPort to port last night. Restore the startup by reading the renamed key.

SECURITY — 500 responses include the full stack trace and file paths, which leaks internals to attackers. Change the error handler in src/server.ts to log the stack and return a generic {"error": "internal error"} body.

DATA LOSS — completing a todo wipes its title. completeTodo in src/todos.ts passes title: undefined to the update, which overwrites the stored title with NULL. Users are losing their data. Keep the existing title when completing.
BUG-020 — GET /todos lists the oldest todos first. Sort by created_at descending in listTodos so the newest appear first.

FEAT-77 — Multi-tenant todos with an external identity provider. Todos must become tenant-scoped: add a tenants table and a tenant_id foreign key on todos, migrate existing rows, authenticate every request against our corporate OIDC provider (new dependency), propagate the tenant claim through every handler, and publish a TodoChanged event to the billing service's new contract so it can meter usage.

BUG-090 — Todo creation times out under load. Replace synchronous inserts with an SQS-backed write queue and a worker service, add a new aws-sdk dependency, change the API to return 202 Accepted with a status URL, and update the mobile client contract accordingly.

BUG-120 — Due dates are lost. Add a due_date column with a migration, change the TodoRow type and every query in src/db.ts and src/todos.ts, update the JSON API contract consumed by the reminders service, and backfill existing rows.

FEAT-80 — Push todo changes to every connected client in real time. Add a WebSocket server (new ws dependency), a pub/sub layer between handlers and connections, reconnect handling, and a new event contract for the web and mobile clients.

FEAT-81 — Move storage from SQLite to Amazon DynamoDB: new data model with partition and sort keys, a migration job for existing rows, a new AWS SDK dependency, and changes to every data-access function.
Small tweak — let users mark todos as high, medium or low priority. Just store the priority with each todo and return it from the API so the apps can show it.
Quick win — GET /todos is a bit slow. Put the list in Redis and serve it from there, invalidating it when a todo changes.
Minor — add Sign in with Google so each user only sees their own todos.
Tidy-up — rename the `done` field to `completed` in all API responses to match the naming the new mobile app uses.
Nice to have — email users the evening before a todo is due.
